title: What is Electromotive Force (emf)?
text:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=mes/iojtphhs

Electromotive force (emf) is the work done per unit charge by any non-conservative forces (chemical reactions inside a battery, or the induced electric field from a changing magnetic flux) that drive current around a closed circuit. Emf is analogous to the mechanical work done by a pump, which creates a pressure difference (analogous to voltage) to cause water to flow even without a height difference.

title: What is Faraday's Flux Rule?
text:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=mes/8k2ag185

Faraday’s flux rule states that a changing magnetic flux through a closed circuit induces an electromotive force (emf) that opposes the change. The main difference from the more general Faraday’s law of induction is that the flux rule applies specifically to closed circuits, while the broader law describes how a changing magnetic field produces a circulating electric field even without a physical circuit.

title: What are Gauss's Laws for Electricity and Magnetism?
text:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=mes/0vkqijjj

Gauss's law states that the divergence of the electric field is proportional to the electric charge density. This means electric field lines diverge away from positive charges and converge towards negative charges. Gauss's law for magnetism states that the divergence of the magnetic field is zero everywhere, so magnetic field lines form closed loops; hence magnetic monopoles should not exist. If they did, the law would have to be modified to include a magnetic charge density term, making it directly analogous to Gauss's law for electricity.

title: What is the Aharonov-Bohm Effect?
text:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1779896694325-22485fc9c91cddb9.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=mes/b9057978)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=mes/b9057978)

The Aharonov–Bohm effect is a quantum phenomenon in which a charged particle’s wavefunction acquires a measurable phase shift when the particle travels through a region where the magnetic field is zero but encloses a confined magnetic flux.

In the standard magnetic version, two coherent charged-particle beams pass along different paths around the flux, and when they recombine, the resulting interference pattern is shifted by an amount determined by the enclosed magnetic flux.
